title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (Part XI of 'Variations sur l'équation des lacets', 'Récapitulation sur les groupes M_{ρ,σ}'). Over a base scheme S we have a form G of GL(2), the derived forms SG and PG, and two sections ρ, σ. They are the canonical lifts of the images of the generators of PSL2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3, normalised by ε0 = -σ^{-1}ρ, ε1 = -ρσ^{-1}, Tr ρ = 1 and Tr σ = 0. G is rigidified so that ε1 = [[1,0],[1,1]]. This gives ρ = [[0,1],[u,1]], σ = [[0,-1],[-u,0]], det ρ = det σ = -u with u a unit, and ε0 = [[1,1/u],[0,1]]. The previous page writes v for u. I checked all of these identities.

This page sets up the building blocks for the group schemes M_{ρ,σ}.

(9) The subgroups are:
- L0, the upper unipotent group;
- L1, the lower unipotent group, which is the conjugate of L0 by σ and also by ρ;
- B'_0 = {[[μ,λ],[0,1]]}, the affine group Aff_1 = G_m ⋉ G_a;
- T0 = {diag(μ,1)}.

(10) B'_0 = T0 ⋉ L0.

(11) Parametrisations ε0(λ) = [[1,λ/u],[0,1]] and ε1(λ) = [[1,0],[λ,1]]. Then ε1(λ) = ρ ε0(λ) ρ^{-1} = σ ε0(λ) σ^{-1}. I verified this: both conjugates equal [[1,0],[uλ,1]] applied to [[1,λ'],[0,1]].

(12) T_ρ and T_σ are the unit group schemes of the rank-2 commutative O_S-algebras O_S[ρ] ≅ O_S[X]/(X²-X-u) and O_S[σ] ≅ O_S[Y]/(Y²-u). These are the characteristic polynomials of ρ and σ. They are Weil-restriction 'tori' R_{A/S}G_m, which are the centralisers of ρ and σ in G. They are genuine tori only where 1+4u, respectively 2u, is invertible; in general they are smooth commutative group schemes.

(13) N'_σ = {g ∈ G : gσg^{-1} = εσ, ε² = 1} ⊂ G, the normaliser of the line O_S σ up to sign.

(14) This gives the extension 1 → T_σ → N'_σ → μ_2 → 1, with ε_σ as the sign character. It is surjective, since diag(1,-1) conjugates σ to -σ.

(15) Products G_{ρ,σ} = B'_0 × T_ρ × T_σ and G*_{ρ,σ} = B'_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ. On the next page these contain M_{ρ,σ}[0], cut out by det u = det b = ±det a, and M_{ρ,σ}(0) ≅ T_{ρ,σ}.

The purpose seems to be an algebraic-group, linear (GL2) model for the symmetries of the pair (ρ,σ): a pair of elements centralising ρ and σ separately plus a Borel-type element, tied together by a determinant/cyclotomic character. This is reminiscent of a 2-dimensional linear shadow of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type action on PSL2(Z)^ (ρ ↦ conjugate of ρ^χ, σ ↦ conjugate of σ). That interpretation is my inference, not stated on the page.
errors: Notational inconsistency: in (9) L0 is written as {[[1,λ],[0,1]]}, while in (11) ε0(λ) = [[1,λ/u],[0,1]]. The sets agree; only the parametrisation differs, and the (11) version is the one making ε1(λ) = σ(ε0(λ)) hold.
The unit is called v on the previous page and u here. (12) is consistent with det ρ = det σ = -u.

Implicit gap: T_ρ and T_σ are tori only where 1+4u (resp. 4u) is invertible. In residue characteristic 2, μ_2 is non-reduced and ±σ coincide, so the sign character in (14) degenerates. The page does not address this; it treats them simply as unit group schemes.

ideas.what: Rigidified matrix model of the generators ρ (order 3 projectively) and σ (order 2 projectively) of PSL2(Z) inside a form of GL2 over an arbitrary base, with unipotent subgroups L0 and L1 exchanged by conjugation by ρ and by σ
ideas.modern_name: standard generators of SL2(Z)/PSL2(Z) in a twisted form of GL2; opposite root subgroups
ideas.where_published: related themes in La Longue Marche (1981, published 2022 edition?) - unsure

ideas.what: Centraliser 'tori' of ρ and σ as unit schemes of the rank-2 algebras O_S[ρ] and O_S[σ]
ideas.modern_name: Weil restriction tori R_{A/S}G_m; centralisers of regular elements in GL2
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 (general theory of tori and centralisers)

ideas.modern_name: normaliser of a maximal torus in GL2, with Weyl group μ_2 / Z/2

ideas.what: Product group schemes G_{ρ,σ} = B'_0 × T_ρ × T_σ and G*_{ρ,σ}, preparing the definition of M_{ρ,σ} by determinant (cyclotomic-type) compatibility conditions
ideas.modern_name: possibly an algebraic/linear analogue of a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type symmetry group of the pair (ρ,σ); no standard name

missed.claim: Grothendieck builds explicit S-group schemes, M_{ρ,σ} via G_{ρ,σ} and G*_{ρ,σ}, attached to the PSL2(Z) generators ρ and σ in a form of GL2 over an arbitrary base. They combine the affine group B'_0 with the centraliser tori of ρ and σ, apparently as a linear algebraic model of the symmetries of the 'équation des lacets'. On this page it is only set-up, and I know of no published counterpart of these specific groups.
missed.quote: On pose (15) G_{ρ,σ} = B'_0 × T_ρ × T_σ, G*_{ρ,σ} = B'_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: If M_{ρ,σ} is meant as a GL2/linearised shadow of GT acting on (ρ,σ), it could connect to work on linear or 'modular' versions of GT and to GT acting on PSL2(Z)^ (Lochak–Schneps, Hain–Matsumoto). This is speculative; the page itself is routine set-up.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine linear-algebraic set-up (unipotent subgroups, centraliser tori, a normaliser extension), and all of it checks out. Mild interest comes only from its role in defining unpublished group schemes M_{ρ,σ}, whose significance is not visible on this page.
transcription_corrections: Under N'_σ in (13) the image shows a vertical inclusion sign followed by G, i.e. N'_σ ⊂ G, not '∩ G_1'.
In (9), λ ∈ Γ G_a; the stray 'is' at the right margin of (9) is probably a marginal mark ('15'?), not part of the formula.
In (12) the crossed-out symbols before T_ρ are an abandoned 'G_{ρ,σ}' heading, and a crossed-out '≃ O_S' appears below. The algebras are A_ρ = O_S + O_S ρ and A_σ = O_S + O_S σ.
Header: 'on considère les sous-groupes'; before (11): 'et [donc] des isos'.
